newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine editor threatened with fake bomb.
newsitem.headline: Argentine editor threatened with fake bomb.

text.p: La Nacion newspaper said on Wednesday its deputy editor had been sent a fake letter-bomb at a time when Argentine news media are on edge because of the murder of a photographer in January.

The 127-year-old newspaper, second largest in the country, said an envelope with plastic explosives, wiring and a battery was sent to Deputy Editor Claudio Escribano on Tuesday with a note warning him: "Next time it's for real."

Escribano, who is also head of the newspaper association ADEPA, was out of the country and the envelope was opened by his secretary, who alerted the police bomb squad. "This is yet another attack on the press," News Editor Ana Donofrio told Reuters. "It is regrettable that these situations keep occurring."

The paper in an editorial said the threat "shows there are still irrational groups in Argentina who are determined to use any means to scare the independent press." But it said such groups were completely wrong to believe they could silence the press using the "terror and violence" so frequent in Argentina's modern history -- especially during the military dictatorship's "Dirty War" of the late 1970s.
Argentina is now a democracy but human rights groups have documented more than 500 threats and attacks on journalists since 1991, including two murders.
The latest fatality was Jose Luis Cabezas, photographer for Noticias magazine, who was handcuffed and shot in January. A former policeman has been arrested for the murder.
A journalist covering the case, Antonio Llorente of television's Channel 13, has received two anonymous threats.
